name: Regions
scope: Regions Bank's US consumer privacy notice, called the Privacy Pledge, read with its Online Privacy Notice and its California privacy disclosure. Incidents count anywhere in the Regions group if they involve the Regions name.

A1.finding: In its sharing table, Regions says it doesn't share your personal information with companies outside the Regions group so they can market to you.
A1.where: Sharing table, row "For nonaffiliates to market to you"

A2.finding: Regions Offers, a cash back scheme with offers from shops, is personalised to your spending habits, and eligible Regions cards are enrolled in it automatically. You can opt out in online banking or the app, and the online notice says you can opt out of rewards programmes and the targeted ads that go with them. Regions says it doesn't give your account, card or other personal information to the shops.
A2.where: Online Privacy Notice, "Use of Information for Advertising"; Regions Offers pages

A3.finding: The online notice says Regions may share personal information with advertising companies it has contracts with, to support its targeted ads, promotions and rewards programmes. You can opt out of the rewards programmes and the targeted ads linked to them. The notice doesn't name social media companies, and Regions' California disclosure says it doesn't share personal information for cross-context behavioural advertising, meaning ads based on what you do on other companies' sites and apps.
A3.where: Online Privacy Notice, "Use of Information for Advertising; Online Behavioral Advertising"

A4.quote: We do not and will not sell or share your personal information.
A4.finding: The promise is in Regions' California privacy disclosure, which also says it hasn't sold or shared personal information covered by California's law in the past 12 months.

A5.quote: Although we may share aggregate information that does not contain personal identifiers.
A5.finding: This is in the sharing table's row about companies outside the Regions group marketing to you. Regions says it doesn't share personal information for that purpose, but it may share this combined, anonymous information. It doesn't say it sells it.
A5.where: Sharing table, row "For nonaffiliates to market to you"

C1.finding: Not measured yet. We count trackers in a real browser, and this check is still to be done.

C2.finding: We couldn't find an Exodus Privacy report for the Regions Android app, com.regions.mobbanking, so this check is still to be done.

C3.finding: Not checked yet. This is checked in a real browser together with the tracker count.

C4.finding: Regions says it uses multi-factor authentication when you log in. If it sees a new device or an unusual login, it sends a one-time code to an email address or phone number it has on file, and you can choose to get a code at every login. Regions has a help page about passkeys, but it doesn't say whether they work for logging in on the website.

D1.finding: The online notice says Regions keeps your information as long as it needs it to do business with you, for the purposes in the notice, or to meet legal duties, settle disputes and enforce agreements. The California disclosure also gives no periods.

D2.finding: The sharing table and the California disclosure list clear types: other Regions companies, joint marketing partners such as insurance companies, credit bureaus, service providers for things like website hosting and data analysis, payment and communication partners, and government agencies.

D3.finding: Neither the online notice nor the California disclosure explains decisions made about you automatically, such as credit or fraud decisions, or how to ask a person to look again. The California disclosure says Regions may draw conclusions from your information to build a profile of you.

D4.finding: The online notice and the California disclosure don't mention artificial intelligence or machine learning, so they don't say whether your data is used to build or train AI models.

E1.finding: To limit direct marketing, the sharing table says to call Regions on 1-800-734-4667, visit a branch or talk to your financial adviser. It gives no online way. You can opt out of the Regions Offers cash back scheme in online banking or the app, but that only covers that scheme.
E1.where: Sharing table, "To limit direct marketing contact"

E2.finding: California residents can ask for a copy of their data with an online Data Request Form or by calling 1-800-986-2462. For other customers, the online notice says you can review and correct some information through your banker or by calling 1-800-240-2948, but it doesn't explain how to get a copy.
E2.where: California disclosure; Online Privacy Notice, "Updating Personal Information You Provide to Us Directly"

incidents.title: Bank employee sold customers' details to fraudsters
incidents.summary: A Regions Bank employee sold customers' names, ID card numbers and account numbers to a group of criminals. Members of the group used fake IDs to pose as customers and withdraw money at Regions branches in Florida, Alabama, Iowa and Missouri in December 2019. Prosecutors said more than 125,000 dollars was stolen, and at least 18 Regions customers were victims of identity theft. Members of the group were sent to prison in February 2023, and the employee pleaded guilty.

notCounted.what: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ordered Regions Bank to pay 191 million dollars over surprise overdraft fees: at least 141 million dollars in refunds and a 50 million dollar penalty.
